verdict.rationale: Alloy documents an Events API that ingests transaction events for real-time or scheduled monitoring through Source Workflows. Customer identity is handled through External Entity IDs, and 206 warnings report missing data. Counterparty identifiers and explicit handling or recovery for rejected input are not documented. Missing for 10: documented counterparty identifier fields on transaction events, validation-error responses and a resubmission/recovery flow for rejected input, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ingest transactions with customer and counterparty identifiers and recover from rejected input

citations.quote: Alloy supports dozens of use cases like interdicting on transactions
any event can be submitted for additional monitoring by mapping the event type to a Source Workflow
Monitors transaction events in real time or at scheduled times to detect suspicious activity
Retroactively Assigning an External Entity ID ... Multiple External Entity IDs
When an Evaluation is in a 206 status, the warnings section in the Evaluation API response and dashboard gives additional information about what data was missing
